section_summary.extract_value: This conclusions section summarizes a single study examining sociocultural influences on mindful eating in college women, reporting that limited appreciation of the body's functional qualities helps explain how family members' self-objectifying body talk negatively affects mindful eating. The authors describe the findings as preliminary and suggest further development and testing of contextual and interpersonal models of adaptive eating styles.
section_summary.evidence_source: Full conclusions text: "The present study provided a novel preliminary partial test of sociocultural theory as applied to mindful eating in college women. Results suggest that limited appreciation of the functional qualities of the body helps explain why vicarious exposure to family members' selfobjectifying body talk exerts a negative influence on mindful eating behavior. Findings may stimulate further development and testing of existing contextual and interpersonal models of adaptive eating styles."
